title: Memory Retrieval under Restricted Context: An Accuracy and Cost Study
research_question: How do file-based project memory and hybrid retrieval compare in answer accuracy and total model cost under equal context-character budgets?

methods.title: File-Based Project Memory
methods.description: The baseline is the actual ProjectMemoryRail. Facts are written to an isolated JIUWENSWARM.md file. Its prompt includes file metadata and is truncated to the full-section character budget. Both arms receive the same facts, questions, model, system prompt and no tools. This is not a retrieval-augmented embedding baseline.

methods.title: Hybrid Selection from Working Memory
methods.description: EnhancedMemoryRail writes completed user-assistant exchanges to process-local L1 memory. The experiment uses lexical Jaccard similarity combined with temporal decay, access frequency and importance, rather than learned embeddings. Selected memories are assembled under the same full-section character budget. The architecture has L2/L3 classes, but this Rail does not route writes there, persist them across process restarts or synchronize a team. MemGPT is conceptual context, not an implemented or tested baseline.

methods.title: Isolation and Cost Accounting
methods.description: Each public-data question has its own fact episode and fresh agents. Baseline writes facts to disk; enhanced performs model-backed memory-writing conversations. The formal question uses a new conversation ID. The runner verifies isolated query history and actual memory injection, alternates arm order across questions, and records both query usage and memory-write usage. Latency including writes is amortized over paired observations. Correctness is accepted-answer string matching; evidence recall requires the complete target fact to survive prompt truncation.

source_notes.longmemeval: Verified source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813, abstract. LongMemEval evaluates long-term conversational memory including extraction, cross-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, updating and abstention. Its design distinguishes indexing, retrieval and reading. This project only adapts a narrow subset and cannot claim coverage of that full evaluation.
source_notes.memgpt: Verified source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560, abstract. MemGPT draws on operating-system memory hierarchies to manage information beyond an LLM context window. It investigates document analysis and multi-session conversation. It motivates memory management conceptually; the present study neither implements nor empirically compares MemGPT.

writing_notes: Describe a small empirical study of the current implementation, not a novel proven multi-level memory system.

Both budgets use the same independent questions from an adapted LongMemEval-S single-session-user slice. Histories are converted into fixed fact episodes with a target answer turn and distractor turns. This is not the official benchmark task.
The smaller budget disadvantages the baseline through truncation and file metadata overhead. Discuss this confound explicitly.
At the larger budget, baseline answer accuracy exceeds complete-evidence recall because a partial fact can still contain the answer.
Emphasize total write-plus-query cost. No error bars or significance claims are justified by one run per budget. These experiments do not validate the automatic paper writer itself.
